Lead numbers halved and each lead cost about 40% more than last period. The lower budget explains part of the drop in numbers, but not the higher cost. We can see three separate problems. The plan to address them starts this week.

Since the period ended: from 26/10 to 01/11 we spent $264.70 for 1 lead, which came in on 26/10. We have had no leads since then.

Ages 35 to 54 did the work

They brought in 8 of the 10 leads at about $120 each. People aged 55+ took 30% of spend for 1 lead, and ads cost far more to show them. That is few leads to judge by. SMSF holders can also skew older, so we want your view before changing anything.

Facebook is doing the work

Facebook brought in 9 of the 10 leads. Instagram cost $219.52 for 1 lead with a much lower CTR, which is why we are pausing it. Men brought in 8 of the 10 leads and took 75% of spend, at a lower cost per lead than women.

What happened and why

Three separate problems

PeriodSpendCPMLink clicksCost per link clickClicks that became leadsLeadsCost per lead
01/09 to 21/09, working well$1,802.13$66.07391$4.615.6%22$81.92
22/09 to 12/10, fewer enquiries$1,361.58$55.50292$4.662.1%6$226.93
13/10 to 01/11, after restructure$769.42$85.53105$7.334.8%5$153.88

1. Fewer people went on to enquire (22/09 to 12/10)

Clicks cost the same, but fewer turned into leads. No one changed the account around 22/09, so we have not confirmed the cause yet. We are testing the form and checking whether the investors most ready to act have already seen the ads.

2. Clicks have cost more (since 12/10)

The campaign was restructured on 12/10 to focus on fewer ads. Cost per link click has since gone from $4.66 to $7.33. ADS 3 VIDEO 1, the ad behind 18 of the 33 leads, has been off since then and is coming back this week.

3. The videos lose people early

The openings are doing their job, with about 21% of people watching past 3 seconds. After that, hold rate has fallen from 28% to 20% and people watch for about 3 seconds on average. The middle of the videos needs to be shorter and simpler.

The budget and what to expect

Budget went from $83 to $38 a day on 29/09, so fewer leads were always likely. Even at the best rate we saw in September (about $82), $38 a day buys about 3 leads a week. That is a sum, not a promise.

Thanks for your lead feedback

You told us you spoke to 11 of the 21 leads from 26/08 to 25/09. Of those, 6 may convert in 3 to 6 months. That matters more than cost per lead alone.

What is running now

One campaign at $38 a day, with one audience (Melbourne + 40km) and an instant form. The two live ads are highlighted above. Since 12/10 in this campaign, ADS 7 VIDEO 1 has cost $78.53 a lead (3 leads) and ADS 3 VIDEO 3 $131.98 a lead (2 leads).

What stands out

The ads with the best hold rate at volume, ADS 4 VIDEO 2 (29.4%) and ADS 3 VIDEO 1 (28.7%), are both paused. The two live ads hold fewer viewers. That is why we are bringing both back this week.

Figures combine every campaign an ad ran in. Average watch and frequency across campaigns are estimates. Not shown: 15 ads with under 1,000 impressions each, $394.55 in total and no leads.

The plan

What we are doing and what we need from you

This week

  1. Bring back ADS 3 VIDEO 1 and ADS 4 VIDEO 2 alongside the two live ads, all in the current campaign so it keeps its history.
  2. Run on Facebook only for now. Instagram has had $144.20 since 13/10 with no leads.
  3. Test the instant form end to end, from a phone through to the lead reaching you.
  4. Clear the six ads Meta has not approved.

Over the next 2 to 3 weeks

  1. Re-edit the existing footage to 15 to 20 seconds, keeping the openings and bringing the offer forward.
  2. Test your best ever ad, Edited Video Ads 3 ($11.19 and $30.19 a lead in April), once its claims are checked against the new rules.

What we need from you

  1. Lead update: fill in the two columns on page 5 and tell us if any of the 6 from last time have moved ahead. If people are hard to reach, we will look at the follow-up.
  2. Target: what can you afford to pay per lead, based on what a settled client is worth to you? We will measure every ad against that number.
  3. Sign-off: a quick approval on the re-edited videos and the older ad, as they run under your credit rep number.
  4. Budget: we suggest holding at $38 a day until cost per lead improves, then talking about raising it. Let us know if that does not suit.
  5. Age: are people aged 55+ a good fit for you? If not, we will trim them from the audience.

Next update

We will report back on Monday 16/11 with how the changes went.
